subject: Information Theory
title: Frequency Modulation
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Frequency Modulation.

hook.text: FM radio sounds clearer than AM in a thunderstorm. The secret: information is in the frequency, not the amplitude.

buildup.text: Frequency modulation varies how fast the carrier wave oscillates. Amplitude stays constant.

discovery.text: Since noise mainly affects amplitude, FM signals resist interference far better than AM signals.

twist.text: FM uses more bandwidth than AM. That wider spectrum is the price for noise resistance. Another Shannon tradeoff.

climax.text: FM broadcasts, emergency radios, and aviation communication all rely on FM's noise resilience.

punchline.text: Vary the speed, ignore the volume. Noise can't touch it.

quiz.question: Why is FM more noise-resistant than AM?
options: Information is in frequency, which noise doesn't easily affect
